newsitem.title: USA: General Cocoa sees Ivory arrivals 340,000 to Dec 7.
newsitem.headline: General Cocoa sees Ivory arrivals 340,000 to Dec 7.

text.p: Total cumulative Ivory Coast cocoa arrivals through December 7 were "guesstimated" at around 340,000 tonnes compared with an estimated 480,000 tonnes at the same date last year, General Cocoa said.

"However, once again, estimates of higher arrivals circulated, with some sources estimating the cumulative arrivals through December 7 in excess of 375,000 tonnes," General Cocoa said in its weekly newsletter.
The total Ivory Coast main crop is currently estimated at 850,000 to 900,000 tonnes, they said, with reports of scattered rains in the cocoa growing regions expected to benefit the 1997 mid crop.
General Cocoa noted, however, it remains too early for any reliable preliminary estimates.

Total 1996/97 Ivorian sales were estimated at around 785,000 tonnes, General Cocoa said, including a guesstimated portion of price-fixing completed against the long term cocoa bean contract with a leading trade house and price-fixation concluded against cocoa products contracts.
They said total Ivory Coast 1997/98 sales are estimated at around 110,000 tonnes, including an estimated small portion of price-fixing completed against outstanding contracts.
